EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows two dominant bands at 1733 cm⁻¹ and 1642 cm⁻¹. 1733 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of an ester C=O stretch, while 1642 cm⁻¹ fits a C=C stretch of a terminal vinyl group.  Additional strong vinyl CH₂ out-of-plane bends appear at 914–955 cm⁻¹ and 1015 cm⁻¹, matching the vinyl moiety. The band at 611 cm⁻¹ is typical for C–O–C skeletal motions of alkyl/allyl esters. Peaks at 2938, 3005, 3056 and 3124 cm⁻¹ correspond to aliphatic and vinylic C–H stretches, while bands at 1302/1327, 1382, 1407 and 1442 cm⁻¹ match CH₃/CH₂ bending modes expected for a molecule containing one methyl group attached to an olefinic carbon. Among the candidates, structure 1 (C=COC(=O)C(=C)C) uniquely contains both an ester carbonyl and a terminal vinyl group, giving the observed 1733 cm⁻¹ (νC=O) and 1640 cm⁻¹ (νC=C) bands together with the vinyl CH₂ wagging modes near 910–1000 cm⁻¹. Candidates bearing nitro (5), multiple carbonyls (6–8), halogens (7, 9, 10) or lacking an ester (2) would generate additional or shifted bands (e.g., strong 1550 cm⁻¹ ν_as(NO₂), ∼1850 cm⁻¹ acyl-F/Cl, or aromatic bands) that are absent here. Therefore candidate 1 best explains the experimental Raman features.
